text:
Maya: Quick flag 1 candidates had emails show up from resume PDFs after the nightly ATS import. Seems like PDF XMP metadata is preserved.

Liam: Yikes. Do we know if this came from our S3 ingest or the third-party resume parser?

Maya: Initial check shows the import payload included an attachments.metadata field with "/Author: recruiter@example.com" entries. I grabbed one sanitized payload.

Rosa: Short term: we should block forwarding of attachments to interview kits and add a recruiter note not to upload original scans.

Liam: Longer term: add a sanitize step in import-service to strip XMP with exiftool or pdfcpu. Feature-flag it for private deployments. I can do a small PR.

Maya: Can you also add a smoke test that uploads a PDF with XMP and asserts attachments.metadata is empty after import?

DevOps-bot: [alert] import-service: 8 files failed metadata-scan (rule: pdf-xmp). Report: https://internal/reports/1901234567/scan.csv

Rosa: I'll run a 10-min recruiter huddle tomorrow 9:30am PT and send a one-paragraph how-to for saving a flattened PDF (Mac Preview / Print -> Save as PDF).

Liam: I'll prototype a lambda that runs exiftool and rewrites the object to S3. Will post branch by EOD.

Maya: Action items: Liam PR + smoke test; Rosa comms + temporary policy; Maya to file incident and loop in Legal if required. Thanks all.
